<description>
This adds a callback hook to the kernel library C header for getting the current script evaluation state on each script evaluation step. This can be used for debugging scripts and gives external applications a view into how Bitcoin Core does script evaluation.

The initial sketch for this work was prepared on rust-bitcoinkernel: https://github.com/sedited/rust-bitcoinkernel/tree/feature_script_debug . That branch also includes a very rudimentary script debugger showcasing the use case for this patch. Clankers seems to do a decent job at coding up prototypes for more featureful debuggers, which seems like a fun project to hack on if anybody else wants to give it a try.

This feature is gated behind the ENABLE_SCRIPT_TRACE flag. To compile with the feature enabled, pass `-DENABLE_SCRIPT_TRACE=ON`. If the feature is not manually enabled, the trace hooks are stubbed out.

The traces are divided into separate frames. RAII is used to guarantee that every script evaluation has at least its start and end state captured. Each instruction generates a unique frame as well.

The ScriptError in the VerifyScript invocation run when calling script_pubkey_verify is added in order to be able to surface the error code in the trace frames.

Another use case could also be using the frames to ensure that the script interpreter is actually doing what we think it is doing during the script tests. This might prevent unit test bugs in the future, i.e. when [error conditions shadow actual behaviour](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/33961), and could also be interesting for fuzzing the script interpreter.
</description>

[2026-11-12] rc:4552808620 inline on src/kernel/bitcoinkernel.h by stringintech (member) (edited 2026-11-12):
To find where a failed evaluation went wrong, a consumer currently has to cross-check the end frame's `opcode_pos` against the last step frame's, and then against the error code, since both codes below are also set from inside the loop:

| error | end pos == last step pos | end pos == last step pos + 1 |
|---|---|---|
| `SCRIPT_ERR_BAD_OPCODE` | executed a bad opcode | failed to decode the opcode at end pos |
| `SCRIPT_ERR_UNBALANCED_CONDITIONAL` | stray `OP_ELSE`/`OP_ENDIF` | missing `OP_ENDIF` (post-loop check, no opcode at fault) |
| any other | failed executing that opcode | — |

The end frame's `opcode_pos` looks like a position in every case, but after the loop completes (success or the post-loop check) it is really the opcode count.

Would it be simpler to let the end frame answer this directly? Every return inside the loop is a failure at the current `opcode_pos`, so the scope only needs to know whether the loop completed, e.g. via a one-line `SCRIPT_TRACE_LOOP_DONE()` right after the try/catch. Then the end frame could report:

- loop not completed: `opcode_pos` is the opcode at which evaluation failed (decoding or executing it)
- loop completed: `opcode_pos` is `0xFFFFFFFF` (no opcode at fault), same convention as `codeseparator_pos`

And then for the getter doc:

```suggestion
/**
 * @brief Get the index of the opcode under evaluation (step frames) or at which
 * evaluation failed (end frames).
 *
 * Counts opcodes, not bytes. A failure can happen while decoding or executing
 * the opcode. End frames report 0xFFFFFFFF if no opcode is at fault: either
 * evaluation succeeded, or it failed in a check after the last opcode (e.g. a
 * missing OP_ENDIF), in which case the end frame's script error is set.
 *
 * @param[in] frame Non-null.
 * @return          The opcode index, or 0xFFFFFFFF.
 */
 BITCOINKERNEL_API uint32_t btck_script_trace_frame_get_opcode_pos(
    const btck_ScriptTraceFrame* frame) BITCOINKERNEL_ARG_NONNULL(1);
```
Going one step further: if the scope keeps a reference to `opcode` (as suggested in my other comment), the end frame could also report the opcode at fault, and `0` when no opcode is at fault (success or post-loop failure). On a decode failure `GetScriptOp` has already set `opcode` to `OP_INVALIDOPCODE`, so the end frame would report `0xff` there.
